newsitem.title: CHINA: Patience key in hostage crisis-Peru congress head.
newsitem.headline: Patience key in hostage crisis-Peru congress head.

text.p: Patience is the key element in solving Peru's hostage crisis in which 72 people have been held by Marxist rebels for 112 days, the president of the country's congress, Victor Joy Way, said on Wednesday.
"Our enemy is not time," he said.
"We have to avoid fixing a specific date for a conclusion, the key element is patience. The first to lose patience will have less opportunity for a solution," he told reporters.
Joy Way, in Shanghai to attend a meeting of the International Chamber of Commerce, said the Peruvian government wanted a peaceful solution to the crisis.
But this in no way included giving in to the rebels' demands for the release of their comrades-in-arms from prison, he said.

"A solution has to be according to our national law and according to international principles and does not include in any way the release of prisoners already imprisoned, sentenced under Peruvian law," Joy Way said.

A crack team of 20 heavily-armed rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) burst into a cocktail party thrown by Japanese Ambassador to Lima Morihisa Aoki on December 17 and took more than 500 guests hostage.

Most captives were released but the rebels hung onto those considered their best bargaining chips including Aoki, two Peruvian government ministers, Fujimori's brother, the Bolivian ambassador and two dozen Japanese businessmen and diplomats.
Joy Way said he was on his way to the party when he received word of the assault on the embassy.
"There was only a five minute delay or I would be one of them," he said, adding that his aide-de-camp is still among those held.
